text:
devon: Uploaded a perfetto trace for the e2e latency spike we saw earlier (client->gateway->runtime). link: https://perfetto.dev/trace/7a2f9c (private). Can folks take a quick look?

maria: grabbing it now. which test? dev or staging?

devon: staging, load ~120rps, single-shot completion avg 45ms but tail went to 800ms for ~1% of requests. trace id 7a2f9c.

sam: opened. I see gateway span followed by a long idle before runtime recv. looks like kvcache miss cascade?

anya: perfetto shows multiple kernel switches inside runtime after request arrives — NV kernels: matmul_qkv_small, matmul_qkv_large, softmax_fp16_fallback. timings: many small kernels then one big FP32 slow kernel ~120ms.

maria: did you run nsys on the same workload? nvprof/nsys would help confirm kernel names and SM utilization.

devon: yes, ran nsys on a single replica with perf record. snippet:
```
nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda --sample=none -o run1 nsys_target_cmd
# exported cpu+cuda timeline
```
I added nvtx markers for request start/finish and kvcache hit/miss.

sam: looking at nsys: the long kernel is "attention_forward_fp32" and its SM occupancy is low, but it fires after a fallback path where the runtime chooses a different kernel set. kernel selection decision logged at: runtime/kernel_selector.cc:214.

anya: timeline correlation: gateway -> client_gw_send -> runtime_recv -> (kv lookup) -> kernel_selector -> kernel_launch sequence. When kvcache has layered misses (prefix miss -> longer KV fetch), kernel_selector chooses a conservative FP32 path to avoid precision bugs. That path is much slower at short batch sizes.

maria: batch size distribution? If most requests are single-turn, batching heuristic might keep batch=1 too long. What were the batching thresholds?

devon: default heuristics: max_batch_time=8ms, prefer_latency=true. Under this load, autobatcher often fires with batch=1. But when KV miss occurs, it inserts ~30-80ms of IO before letting kernels run, so the runtime re-evaluates kernel choice and picks FP32.

sam: so it's an ordering problem: delayed KV IO changes the context for kernel selection (sequence length estimate or quantization profile) and runtime picks slower kernels mid-flight. That matches the sudden tail.

anya: I captured a perfetto slice where kernel_selector logged: "selected kernel_set=fp32_safe (reason=kv_miss_precaution)" right before the 120ms kernel.

maria: do we have a repro where we force kv miss artificially? could add a warmup stage to isolate.

devon: yes, I ran a deterministic repro: 1000 requests with keys not in cache. median latency 90ms, tail 700ms. If I prepopulate kvcache, tail disappears.

sam: proposed mitigations: 1) make kernel selection decision sticky for request lifetime (prevent mid-request switch), 2) change heuristic to bias quantized kernels even when kv misses if sequence length matches, 3) warm prefetch of KV for likely prefixes.

anya: also consider doing the kernel selection based on metadata available at enqueue time instead of at launch time. small change: evaluate selection in enqueue path where we still have original inference context.

maria: ops note: for Dedicated customers we could offer "pin kernel profile" flag to avoid runtime re-eval for sensitive workloads.

devon: I ran nvprof too; summary: FP32 kernel had 5x higher time per token and 3x lower tensor core utilization. nvprof output: 
```
GPU activities:
  attention_forward_fp32  calls: 1  time: 118ms  SM%: 22  tensor_cores: low
  attention_qkv_cuda     calls: 8  time: 15ms   SM%: 78  tensor_cores: high
```

sam: that confirms the perf delta. Also saw context-switch overhead when kernel_set changes frequently across bursts — small but accumulates.

anya: small experiment idea: when a KV miss is detected, we can enqueue a lightweight placeholder to keep batch assembly consistent then continue KV fetch in parallel, so kernel selection doesn't see the temporary state. Could reduce mis-selection.

maria: can you sketch a patch? if it's low-risk we can roll to staging.

devon: I have a WIP branch: runtime/batcher:sticky_kernel_selection_v1. It computes kernel_set at enqueue and stores it in request metadata. If enqueue lacks certainty we mark as "deferred" and fall back to default quantized selection. Early tests: tail reduced from 800ms -> 120ms worst.

sam: nice. does it change memory for cache keys? any additional CPU impact?

devon: minimal CPU, adds 16 bytes per request for metadata. Batching path unchanged.

anya: we should add a perfetto trace before/after patch and nvprof sampling. Also add a unit test forcing kv miss path to assert kernel_set chosen is quantized.

maria: I'll pick up test + rollout plan. Can you upload the before/after perfetto traces to the internal bucket and link here?

devon: uploaded: before: https://perfetto.dev/trace/7a2f9c  after: https://perfetto.dev/trace/7a5b3d (staging).
Also put nsys logs in //s3/rw-inference/perf/1917654321/.

sam: CI note: add a perf regression check to fail if tail p99 grows >20% for single-shot workloads in nightly.

maria: agreed. Also flagging product: might be surprising for customers on Dedicated.

infra-bot: Deploy job started for runtime/batcher:sticky_kernel_selection_v1 to staging (job 4021). :rocket:

devon: thanks. I'll monitor perfetto traces during rollout and ping here if anything weird.

maria: great work. summary for changelog? short line: "Make kernel selection sticky at enqueue time to avoid KV-miss induced FP32 fallbacks and reduce tail latency." :white_check_mark:

sam: merging notes: watch for increased latency on very long-seq workloads where FP32 was chosen for correctness; add opt-in flag for strict correctness path.

anya: tagging this thread with #perfetto #nsys #kvcache. will follow up with a short doc on the heuristic change.

devon: end.
